original_question: What is the length, in amino acids, of the mature form of the protein that is mutated in the condition characterized by the excessive breakdown of elastin due to protease imbalance?

final_qi.question: What is the length, in amino acids, of the mature form of the protein that is mutated in the condition characterized by the excessive breakdown of elastin due to protease imbalance?
final_qi.long_answer: Excessive elastin breakdown in the lung, as seen in α-1 antitrypsin deficiency, results from mutations in the SERPINA1 gene encoding α-1 antitrypsin (AAT), a serine-protease inhibitor that normally neutralizes neutrophil elastase. The AAT precursor contains a 24-residue signal peptide; after its removal, the secreted mature protein comprises 394 amino acids. Hence, the length of the mature α-1 antitrypsin molecule is 394 amino acids.

final_answer.long_answer: Alpha-1 antitrypsin (mutated in the protease–antiprotease imbalance that causes excessive elastin degradation and emphysema) is synthesized as a 418-residue precursor with a 24-residue signal peptide. Removal of this signal sequence yields the mature secreted protein, which is 394 amino acids long.

final_answer.long_answer: The disease caused by a protease–antiprotease imbalance leading to excessive elastin degradation is α-1 antitrypsin deficiency. The affected gene (SERPINA1) encodes the serpin α-1 antitrypsin. After removal of its 24-residue signal peptide, the secreted mature α-1 antitrypsin polypeptide consists of 394 amino acids.
